subject: Datacove POC follow-up: recommended model slate and operational asks
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Briggs <alex@datacove.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Datacove POC follow-up: recommended model slate and operational asks

Hi Alex — great to meet today, thanks for the walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and a suggested short list for the POC plus operational asks so procurement and engineering can align.

Top-line recommended slate (tradeoffs summarized):

1) redwood-rt-7B-q4_0 (recommended baseline)
- Why: best cost/latency balance for majority of Datacove’s user flows (summary generation, short Q&A).
- Expected perf: median latency ~35–50ms/token on our hosted region, 95p typically under 120ms for 128-token outputs (subject to request shape).
- Cost: lowest unit cost with q4_0 quantization.
- Risk: occasional quality misses on very long context or niche domain language.

2) open-axiom-13B-f32 (quality-first option)
- Why: stronger factuality and fewer hallucinations on long-form prompts; good when correctness > cost.
- Expected perf: higher latency (~2–3x vs 7B) and increased token cost.
- Risk: higher cost; may need dedicated capacity for sustained QPS.

3) hybrid fallback pattern (rt-7B baseline + 13B for escalation)
- Why: keep cost/latency efficient for normal traffic and route edge/complex queries to 13B.
- Operational notes: requires routing policy and label-based sampling during POC to collect edge cases.

Benchmarks & assets attached: datacove_poc_benchmarks.csv (head-to-head across your sample prompts), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (anonymized sample prompt pack we used), cost-latency-scenarios.pdf (three scaled QPS scenarios). Link also in-line here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example-poc-resources

Quality/regression guardrails we recommend during POC:
- Holdout eval set (you provided ~2k prompts) to run nightly regression checks.
- Regression alerts: precision/recall thresholds plus a small human-review sample for NER/factual tasks.
- Canary rollout: start at 5% ramp to observe user impact before full cutover.
- Prompt-set versioning + deterministic sampling (seeded RNG) for reproducible comparisons.

Operational asks for procurement/engineering to confirm:
- Target sustained QPS and burst QPS (estimate you gave today: 20–40 sustained, 150 bursts) — please confirm.
- Data residency: you flagged EU-sourced PII for future; any immediate constraints for the POC?
- SLA/uptime baseline expectations for dedicated capacity (if you opt for 13B).

Immediate next steps we suggest:
- You: share final 2k prompt set (anonymized) and a real sample of 10 representative longer prompts for 95p latency checks.
- Us: run head-to-head with the attached prompt_set_v1 and produce a short pack with per-prompt diffs + recommended routing rules (ETA 48 business hours after we get the set).
- Procurement: if you want an indicative commercial that includes a small reserved burst package, loop procurement@datacove.ai and we’ll prepare a draft term sheet.

Attachments: datacove_poc_benchmarks.csv, prompt_set_v1.jsonl, cost-latency-scenarios.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up the week of 21st to walk the numbers.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198
From: Alex Briggs <alex@datacove.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@datacove.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Jul 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Datacove POC follow-up: recommended model slate and operational asks

Thanks Monica — this is very helpful. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Can you confirm 95p latency for the rt-7B under our sample distribution when outputs are ~10 tokens vs 128 tokens? Our product path is often short completions ~8–20 tokens and 95p behavior there matters.

- For the hybrid fallback, how would you recommend detecting escalation candidates? We have a proprietary complexity score we can attach to requests — would prefer to have rules rather than ML routing at POC time.

- Procurement question: for the indicative commercial, please include a conservative cost estimate that assumes a 30% cache miss (our caching is optimistic early on).

I’ll loop in procurement and we’ll send over the anonymized 2k prompt set by EOD Monday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alex
Alex Briggs
Head of Product, Datacove
alex@datacove.ai

Alex — thanks, that timeline works. Two quick clarifications and a proposed next step: 

1) 95p latency slices: we’ll report separate numbers for short (8–20 tokens) and long (64–128 tokens). For rt-7B baseline we expect 95p for short outputs <70ms in our region but will validate on your set (we’ll flag any geographic variation).

2) Escalation detection: agree to start with deterministic rule-based routing using your complexity score threshold + a fallback heuristic (longer user history + presence of named entities). We’ll include the exact rule set in the routing doc.

Proposed next step — schedule a 30-min sync to review benchmarks once we finish the head-to-head. I’m available Wed 16 Jul 10:00–11:30 PT or Thu 17 Jul 13:00–15:00 PT. If one of those works, I’ll share a calendar invite and a short 1-pager (attached) summarizing the canary plan and cost sensitivity.

We’ve attached prompt_set_v1.jsonl for your reference and included the benchmark template; we’ll run the head-to-head as soon as we have your 2k pack.

Thanks — speak soon.

—Monica
